_about: Showcase sources for this project's website (landing direction D), cut by .github/workflows/showcase.yml. Times are seconds in the NASA original. Licences and the reasons for every cut: docs/saas/landing-d-sources.md. A source is cut only when approved is true and sha256 is pinned; every source gets a vetting pack. cut_on_push controls whether a push spends an AI run on it.

black_holes.title: Shedding Light on Black Holes

crop.why: removes the persistent 'science @ NASA' insignia bug (top right, x 1650-1852, y 63-147 of 1920x1076) and the Event Horizon Telescope logo (top left on EHT frames); keeps the right-aligned image credits

segments.why: after the Science@NASA bumper and the science.nasa.gov screenshots (their crossfade's last ghost frame is 20.033 s); intro and myth 1

myth 3. Drops 84.2-138.6 (myth 2): an artwork credited Robin Dienel, Carnegie Institution for Science, licence unverified; narration naming and quoting Dr. Dan Evans (NASA Headquarters) over his photo card
outro. Drops 174.3-203.95 (myth 4): Stephen Hawking's photo and name card appear before its sentence ends. Ends before 'visit science.nasa.gov' and the NASA end card

black_holes.caption_detector_override_why: the myth 3 title card prints its spoken sentence for ~13 s and lands on one of subtitles.already_captioned's eight sample frames; it is a title, not running captions. The detector's real verdict is still logged to already_captioned_verdict.json

eye_on_neptune.title: Eye on Neptune
eye_on_neptune.insignia_bug: 'science @ NASA' with the NASA insignia, top right from 12 s to 2:56, x ~1635-1840, y ~55-142 of 1900x1068 (measured from the vetting pack's corner strips). No single 16:9 window clears it: a window below it is at most 1624 px wide, and the kept shots carry credits or labels at both edges. So each segment gets the treatment its frames allow.

segments.why: 'It is an ice giant, a planet of monster storms, and a recluse rarely seen.' Speech 14.76-21.07 (-60 dB pauses 13.85-14.76 and 21.07-21.73). The Science@NASA wordmark is still faintly visible at 14.19 and gone by 14.29; 'September 9th' is drawn at ~22 s. Crop window left-aligned below the bug (dense starfield here, where delogo leaves a visible streak) keeps the left 'Artist Rendering' credit and the planet.

'Voyager 2 provided our closest glimpse ...' to '... observations of the planet from afar.' Speech 98.91-128.84. Drops 21.40-98.49: the dated opposition lines ('on the night of September 9', 'evenings in September', 'the 30th anniversary'), stargazer silhouettes and a person at a computer, and 64.6-69.6 Stellarium sky frames (Stellarium allows non-profit/CC use only) under a sentence that cannot be cut around. Crop window right-aligned below the bug: the Voyager photos pass under the bug at 1:50-1:58, where delogo would smear them; keeps the right-aligned credits. Ends before the Hubble-to-Neptune dissolve (~129.0).

'Scientists have determined that Neptune has seasons ...' to '... including right here on Earth.' Speech 139.86-161.34. Drops 128.90-139.44: 'NASA scientists have learned ...'. Full frame with delogo over the bug (black or sparse-star corner here; checked invisible on black at 149 s), because the 1996/1998/2002 labels sit at the left edge and the Sromovsky/Fry credit at the right. Ends before the dissolve into a Stellarium sky (~161.6) and before 'consider taking a look ... in September'.

eye_on_neptune.caption_detector_override_why: the vetting pack's contact sheets and credit bands show no burned-in speech captions in the kept ranges (only image credits and the year labels 1996/1998/2002); a false positive would strip our captions from every clip, so the driver keeps them. The detector's real verdict is still logged to already_captioned_verdict.json
